clue.text: Get engaged to make setter quiet

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as me
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone getting engaged in order to make a crossword compiler shut up.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear wheels mesh when their teeth interlock, which is the mechanical sense of getting engaged.

clue.text: Experiment that pays lawyers to make it?

definitions.text: that pays lawyers to make it?

explanation.surface: A test case set up mainly to keep the legal profession in fees.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads the phrase literally: a run of trials in court is what keeps lawyers paid.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial run is a preliminary test before real use, an experiment; read literally, a run of court cases keeps lawyers in fees.

clue.text: Male entry for church appointment

indicators.note: the letters make their entry at the start of the phrase church appointment, running across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A man's name being put forward for a post in the church.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordius may intend CH (church) plus AP, the start of appointment; either way the letters sit at the front of church appointment.
explanation.definitionFit: Chap is an informal word for a man or fellow, so a male person.

clue.text: THE thing that will go off …

parts.note: read the answer as wordplay: time abbreviates to T and a bomb is HE, high explosive, so together they spell the capitalised word

explanation.surface: Capitals stress that this is the one device everyone fears will explode.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: T is the standard abbreviation for time and HE (high explosive) stands for a bomb, so the two parts of the answer shrink to the printed word.
explanation.definitionFit: A device set to explode at a fixed moment is a thing that will go off when the clock runs down.

clue.text: … has gone off

parts.note: following on from the bomb that will go off, going off here means dropping into slumber rather than exploding

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, something has finally exploded.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to the time bomb, steering toward an explosion, but to go off also means to fall into sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has gone off has dropped into slumber and is now sleeping.

clue.text: Spooner's window ledge blackened, which is unlucky

indicators.note: Spooner signals a swap of sounds between the two words that follow

parts.note: a window ledge is a sill
something coated with tar has been tarred, so blackened

explanation.surface: A window ledge painted black, which brings bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: Not a true Spoonerism: no initial sounds swap; the S of the first word simply moves to the start of the second, giving the hyphenated answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being born under an evil star means being doomed to misfortune, so unlucky.

clue.text: Discovered rental scam

indicators.note: a scam is a swindle, a dishonest working, which signals the letters of rental being worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone has found out about a fraudulent letting arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: To have learnt something is to have found it out, a past-tense synonym of discovered.

clue.text: Came across single turning into a pair

indicators.note: turning signals that the combined letters of came across and single are read backwards

parts.note: to meet someone is to come across them, so came across is met
I is the Roman numeral one, so single

explanation.surface: Someone met a single person who then became half of a couple.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple in a romantic relationship are called an item, so a pair.

clue.text: Shortage when Germany lost ground

indicators.note: lost signals that the letter for Germany is taken away

parts.note: a dearth is a shortage or scarcity
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A scarcity arose after Germany gave up territory.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth means soil or the land underfoot, a synonym for ground.

clue.text: Lacking respect over neckline showing bust

indicators.note: over signals the disrespectful word lying across and around the neckline letter

parts.note: insolent means rude and lacking respect
a V is a common shape of neckline, the V-neck

explanation.surface: A rude remark about a low neckline that reveals the bosom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust' looks like part of the cleavage picture, but it means bankrupt.
explanation.definitionFit: Going bust means becoming bankrupt, unable to pay debts.

clue.text: Ice heaped over protective wear

indicators.note: over in the sense of knocked over signals the letters of ice heaped being upset into a new order

explanation.surface: Ice piled on top of a layer of protective clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A headpiece is a helmet or other covering for the head, worn for protection.

clue.text: A lot of cider seen at Twickenham?

indicators.note: a lot of, but not all, signals that the cider word loses its last letters

parts.note: scrumpy is rough farmhouse cider from the West Country

explanation.surface: Plenty of cider being drunk by fans at a rugby ground.
explanation.walkthrough: TWICKENHAM is the home stadium of English rugby union, where a scrum is a regular sight.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrum is the set piece of rugby, routinely seen at the national rugby stadium.

clue.text: Country has two senior officers to 1,000 men

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers or men
OC is officer commanding, one senior officer
CO is commanding officer, the second senior officer

explanation.surface: A nation where a thousand soldiers are led by a pair of high-ranking officers.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces go in answer order: the thousand and the men first, then the two officers, OC then CO.
explanation.definitionFit: Morocco is a kingdom in north-west Africa, so a country.

clue.text: French word and choral work

parts.note: mot is the French for word
et is the French for and, the French carrying over

explanation.surface: A French term and a piece for choir.
explanation.definitionFit: A motet is a short sacred composition for voices, a choral work.

clue.text: Wild chase to forest to provide a protective cover

indicators.note: wild signals the letters of chase running out of control into a new order

parts.note: Arden is a forest in Warwickshire, the setting of As You Like It

explanation.surface: A frantic pursuit into the woods to find shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: To case-harden metal is to give it a hard outer layer, a protective cover.

clue.text: Colonial settler parking with no rear light

indicators.note: with no rear signals the last letter of the light being dropped

parts.note: a lantern is a light

explanation.surface: A colonist leaves his car without a working tail light.
explanation.definitionFit: A planter was a settler in a colony, especially one who ran a plantation.

clue.text: Limb lopped at stock farm

indicators.note: lopped signals cutting off the first letter, as a limb is lopped from a tree

parts.note: a branch is a limb of a tree

explanation.surface: A tree limb cut back on a cattle farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranch is a large farm for raising livestock, so a stock farm.

clue.text: A number wearing clothes seen by the fire

indicators.note: wearing signals the clothes going around the number letter

parts.note: togs is informal for clothes
N is the algebraic symbol for a number

explanation.surface: Someone sitting fully dressed beside the fireplace.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongs are the pincers kept on the hearth for handling coal, so found by the fire.

clue.text: Rotten fish cast back

indicators.note: cast back signals the fish word being read backwards

parts.note: a dab is a small flatfish

explanation.surface: A putrid fish thrown back into the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad describes food that has gone off, a synonym for rotten.

clue.text: English marred a part of Guyana

annotationWithheld.why: English marred a part of Guyana: the anagram of E + MARRED + A has no indicator unless marred does double duty as fodder and signal, which the check refuses
annotationWithheld.clue: English marred a part of Guyana

clue.text: Hood for one born illegitimately

indicators.note: illegitimately, outside the rules, signals the letters being arranged irregularly

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An outlaw described as a child born out of wedlock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hood for one' looks like the definition by example, but 'one' supplies the I; Hood alone indicates the outlaw by his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary outlaw of Sherwood is named by his surname alone, so his first name stands for him.

clue.text: Dress up with good skill and one can boast

indicators.note: up in a down clue signals the dress word being read from bottom to top

parts.note: garb means clothing or dress
art means skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: Someone who dresses smartly and has real talent may well show off.
explanation.definitionFit: A braggart is a person who brags, so someone given to boasting.

clue.text: What's reflected in 29 building maliciously ruined

indicators.note: reflected, as in a mirror, signals reading the gallery's contents backwards

parts.note: what is in 29, the Tate gallery, is art
a shed is a simple building

explanation.surface: An image reflected in the gallery building, which vandals wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 29 is the Tate, the London art gallery, so what's in it is art.
explanation.definitionFit: Trashed means wrecked or vandalised, so deliberately ruined.

clue.text: Witness occasion of deliberate no-balls?

explanation.surface: Testifying about a cricket match where bowlers overstepped on purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as AT TEST: at a Test match, the scene of a 2010 cricket betting scandal in which Pakistani bowlers deliberately bowled no-balls.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness or certify truth; split as AT TEST, it locates a Test match where the deliberate no-balls happened.

clue.text: Fed up? Scoff and overcome …

indicators.note: up in a down clue signals the word fed being read from bottom to top

parts.note: to scoff food is to eat it greedily

explanation.surface: Someone sick of it all stuffs their face and is defeated.
explanation.definitionFit: To defeat an opponent is to overcome them.

clue.text: Remedy after thaw — dumb play with comic hat

indicators.note: play signals the letters of dumb being played around with
comic signals the letters of hat being arranged absurdly

explanation.surface: A mime act in a funny hat performed when the snow melts.
explanation.walkthrough: A thaw leaves mud everywhere, and a soak in mud is a spa treatment, hence remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A mud bath is a therapeutic soak in mud, a spa remedy, and mud is what a thaw leaves.

clue.text: Parking accessory with cops needing hesitation

parts.note: the Met is the Metropolitan Police of London
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Police hesitating over a parking device.
explanation.definitionFit: A parking meter is the coin-operated device beside a parking space, so a parking accessory.

clue.text: … as is the fashion at organised demo

indicators.note: organised signals the letters of demo being arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Following on, a protest march has become the latest trend.
explanation.definitionFit: A mode is a prevailing style, so the current fashion.

clue.text: What Blair lacked in reported saga?

indicators.note: reported signals that the saga's name is said out loud

parts.note: The Forsyte Saga is the novel sequence by John Galsworthy

explanation.surface: A dig at a prime minister's failings, as described in a long story.
explanation.walkthrough: Blair is Tony Blair, UK prime minister until 2007, whose lack of planning for Iraq was widely criticised.
explanation.definitionFit: Foresight is the ability to anticipate consequences, which critics said the former prime minister lacked.

clue.text: It's said to spot the spot

indicators.note: said signals that the word for spotting is heard rather than read

parts.note: to sight something is to spot it

explanation.surface: A riddle claiming a word means both noticing a place and the place itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a location, the spot where something is.

clue.text: Picture show from 19 proceeds?

parts.note: an art gallery founded on the profits of demerara sugar, the answer to 19

explanation.surface: An art exhibition paid for by the sale of sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Tate of the sugar refiners Tate & Lyle funded the London gallery that bears his name.
explanation.definitionFit: The London gallery was paid for by a sugar magnate, so it is a picture show funded by sugar.

clue.text: Neglected state of Paris with dire confusion

indicators.note: confusion signals the letters of the two words being muddled together

explanation.surface: The French capital in a dreadful muddle and falling apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Disrepair is the condition of something poorly maintained, so a neglected state.

clue.text: Without a red card?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside signals the red word wrapping around the a

parts.note: a Trot, a Trotskyist, is a red

explanation.surface: A footballer escapes a red card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red card' is a football picture, but red is a Trotskyist, TROT, and card the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarot is one of the cards of the fortune-telling pack, hence the question mark for card.
